messages:
maria: Heads-up — started seeing intermittent 30s call timeouts in the Android sample when the auth token expires mid-request. Only on devices, not emulator. Logs show requests stuck in QUEUED for a long time then the call timeout fires.

sam: hmm. QUEUED -> usually dispatcher saturation or connection reuse issues. Which client config? timeouts?

maria: default OkHttp via our SDK wrapper. No custom dispatcher. Call timeout set to 30s. connect/read/write are 10/30/30. Happens when multiple uploads + token refresh races.

jonathan: do we use OkHttp Authenticator to refresh tokens? If the authenticator makes a blocking request on the same client, that can deadlock the dispatcher (authenticator runs on network thread).

maria: yes we do. our Authenticator does: `val resp = client.newCall(tokenReq).execute()` then writes new token to shared prefs and returns newRequest.

sam: that's probably it. Authenticator is called while a connection is being processed; if the client is reusing the same dispatcher and the token refresh blocks on queued connections, they queue on each other -> starvation. Android device networking is slower so it surfaces there.

alex: short repro I ran: spawn 10 concurrent uploads, force token expiry, then watch all 10 go QUEUED while each Authenticator waits for a response that can't run because threads are eaten.

maria: ugh. any recommended fix? quick patch or SDK change?

jonathan: options:
- Do token refresh outside of OkHttp Authenticator (preferred): have an Interceptor that, on 401, attempts a refresh using a separate OkHttpClient instance dedicated to auth calls. Then retry the original.
- If you must use Authenticator, create a separate client for the refresh call: `val authClient = client.newBuilder().dispatcher(Dispatcher(Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor())).build()` and use that for `authClient.newCall(...).execute()` inside the Authenticator.
- Or increase dispatcher maxRequests and maxRequestsPerHost as a band-aid, but that doesn't address correctness.

sam: +1 for separate client for auth. Also avoid doing heavy synchronous work in the Authenticator — keep it tiny.

maria: quick patch I tried in the sample: switched to a refresh interceptor that uses a small single-shot client. Fixed the QUEUED hang. I'll paste snippet:
```kotlin
class TokenRefreshInterceptor(val authClient: OkHttpClient): Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val req = chain.request()
    val res = chain.proceed(req)
    if (res.code == 401) {
      synchronized(this) {
        // try refresh with separate client to avoid dispatcher deadlock
        val refreshReq = Request.Builder().url("https://auth/refresh").post(...).build()
        val refreshResp = authClient.newCall(refreshReq).execute()
        if (refreshResp.isSuccessful) {
          val newToken = parse(refreshResp)
          // persist token
          val newReq = req.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $newToken").build()
          res.close()
          return chain.proceed(newReq)
        }
      }
    }
    return res
  }
}
```

jonathan: that looks good. Two caveats: be careful with chain.proceed recursion and close original response (you did). Also avoid long blocking refresh on main thread — ensure interceptor runs on network thread (it will).

alex: worth noting: Retrofit's default Call timeout is a wrapper and doesn't prevent dispatcher queuing. We had one case where callTimeout fired but auth refresh still blocking other calls. So set sensible dispatcher and use dedicated auth client.

maria: created small sample branch: sample/android-token-refresh-fix. Repro steps in README: spawn 12 concurrent multipart uploads, expire token, observe queue then fix.

sam: can we add a unit/integration test in our SDK tests that simulates this? maybe a local MockWebServer that delays auth endpoint and asserts no global queue starvation.

ci-bot: created ticket INF-1024 and attached the sample branch link.

jonathan: one more gotcha I ran into — if you create authClient with the same connection pool it can still share resources. Use `connectionPool(ConnectionPool(0, 1, TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS))` or newBuilder without sharing pools, or better: `OkHttpClient.Builder().connectionPool(ConnectionPool())` with a dedicated pool.

maria: noted. I'll update the sample to use dedicated dispatcher + pool for the auth client and add a test that asserts no QUEUED pileup.

alex: tl;dr for SDK docs: add a short section under "Auth integration" about "Avoid blocking token refresh on same client — use dedicated client or interceptor pattern" with code sample. Saves support tickets. :thumbsup:

maria: will send PR with sample + doc tomorrow. Thanks all.

sam: nice catch and great repro steps.

jonathan: fyi we should also audit our Android quickstart — it currently shows an Authenticator example that uses the main client. That's misleading. I'll open a follow-up to update quickstart.

maria: ok will wait on changelog entry until quickstart update lands.

alex: marking resolved for the immediate bug; tracking doc/work item in INF-1024.
